title: Redwood POC weekly sync - quantaco.ai cost econ
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. Reviewed benchmark numbers (tokens/sec and tokens/$) from last run, discussed impact of prefix/KV caching and batching tradeoffs on latency and cost, looked at quantization and model variant routing, and agreed on next benchmarks and deliverables. Agreed AE to send updated pricing and caching docs; SE to run 4k-context throughput tokens-per-dollar test; customer to share production request distribution. Next meeting scheduled 2026-07-01.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Liam O'Connor: yeah liam here.
[00:07] Sana Rizvi: sana on infra.
[00:09] Diego Morales: diego, ct o, sorry fighting wifi, i'm here.
[00:12] Alex Chen: alex from redwood se.
[00:14] Maya Patel: sweet ok goal for today is a focused cost econ review — tokens per second, tokens per dollar, caching effects, batching tradeoffs, then actions.
[00:24] Maya Patel: alex do you want to kick off with the numbers from the recent run?
[00:27] Alex Chen: sure, so we re-ran the 2.7b_v2 model on the 8k baseline workload you sent. rough high level: median latency at batch size=1 was 120ms per token, tokens/sec throughput about 8.3 tps on p4d equivalent; tokens per dollar we calculated by taking the cost bucket for the run — roughly 1.8 million tokens per dollar on hosted profiles with our recommended quantized runtime. those numbers assume no prefix caching.
[00:55] Liam O'Connor: wait 1.8m tokens per dollar seems a bit optimistic — what's included in that calc? is that just GPU runtime or does that include networking and regional egress?
[01:03] Alex Chen: good call — that's compute-only for the GPU runtime, so we excluded infra overhead like egress/storage. If you add a typical networking+controlplane add of ~15%, it drops to ~1.55m tokens/$ in our spreadsheet.
[01:15] Sana Rizvi: and that's with 4-bit quant? or 8-bit? i couldn't remember the flag in the run notes.
[01:19] Alex Chen: that's 4-bit q4_k_mixed actually, which gives a nice perf uplift. we also ran fp16 as a control: fp16 tokens/$ were about 45% lower given higher memory and lower batching efficiency.
[01:33] Diego Morales: how does caching come into play? we have a lot of repeated prompts and long prefixes in prod so if caching buys good savings it could change things a lot.
[01:40] Alex Chen: absolutely — we tested prefix caching and KV cache separately. prefix caching (server-side reuse of common prompt prefixes) saved about 22% of token compute in our trace replay; KV cache for chat context saved up to 40% of forward compute for sessions with lots of repeated tokens. combined we saw an effective tokens/$ improvement from 1.55m to about 2.1m tokens/$.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: that's huge. are those numbers sensitive to session length? our median session is only 120 tokens but we have tails to 4k.
[02:13] Alex Chen: yes it's very distribution-dependent. for short interactions the caching benefit is smaller; for long session tails (2–4k) kv cache is more impactful. we broke it down: for sessions >1k tokens, KV cache saved ~38–42% of compute; for <250 tokens, savings were 8–12%.
[02:31] Maya Patel: wanted to flag latency SLOs. when you start batching aggressively to improve tokens/$, tail latency jumps. alex, did you measure p95/p99 at different batch sizes?
[02:40] Alex Chen: yep. batch size 1 p95 was 230ms, p99 480ms. batch size 8 improved tokens/sec by roughly 3.4x, tokens/$ increased accordingly but p95 moved to ~620ms and p99 approached 1.2s. so there is a clear latency vs cost tradeoff.
[02:58] Sana Rizvi: for our customer-facing product we need p95 < 600ms otherwise okrs suffer. so batch size 8 might be borderline. how about dynamic batching with latency caps?
[03:07] Alex Chen: Redwood runtime supports latency-aware batching: you can set a max wait of e.g., 50ms and a max batch size; that retains most batching gains while bounding added latency. in our config tests, 50ms wait with max batch 8 got us ~2.8x throughput with p95 ~540ms.
[03:26] Diego Morales: what's the tokens/sec/$ delta between static batch8 and dynamic cap?
[03:30] Alex Chen: static batch8 tokens/$ ~2.9m (compute-only), dynamic cap config came to ~2.6m because of slightly smaller avg batch sizes, but p95 gains are why you'd pick it. with prefix+kv caching on top we were at ~3.5m tokens/$.
[03:46] Liam O'Connor: curious about model variants and routing — you mentioned fallback to cheaper variants on high load. is that automated?
[03:52] Alex Chen: you can configure routing policies. we tested routing to a distilled 1.3b variant for non-critical paths which reduces tokens cost by ~45% but has a measurable accuracy delta. Redwood can do A/B routing, fallback tiers, and can apply routing by tag, endpoint, or latency budget.
[04:10] Sana Rizvi: accuracy delta — do you have the eval numbers? production is sensitive to hallucination rate.
[04:15] Alex Chen: we ran your eval set — distilled 1.3b had a 6% regression on our task-specific metrics, so you can do selective routing: route high-confidence or templated prompts to cheap variant.
[04:25] Diego Morales: ok that seems workable. about quantization — are there stability/serving gotchas for q4_k? we've hit tokenization fidelity issues before.
[04:33] Alex Chen: good point. q4_k is stable for most models we ship but we recommend running a small quality validation set; for certain tokens and rounding edge cases, you might prefer q8 or mixed fp16 for a small cost increase. we captured a few edge failures in the run notes (file linked in chat).
[04:47] Maya Patel: can we talk about the spreadsheet you shared? liam, did you have a chance to look at the cost model columns?
[04:51] Liam O'Connor: yeah i skimmed. two questions: 1) you have caching savings as a single multiplier — is that per-session or global? 2) do you model reserved/dedicated pricing vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
[04:59] Alex Chen: caching multiplier is modeled per-session profile (we have low/med/high repeatability). and yes we modeled both hosted and dedicated — dedicated reserved instances lower unit cost about 30–40% depending on commit level, but you take on utilization risk.
[05:12] Sana Rizvi: for us, utilization will start low in pilot so committed reservations are risky. prefer hosted with burst-to-dedicated if possible. does Redwood support that?
[05:20] Alex Chen: yes, we can set routing policies to prefer hosted unless utilization exceeds a threshold, then spill to dedicated pools — or vice versa depending on your preference.
[05:28] Diego Morales: can you walk through an example of tokens/sec/$ with caching + dynamic batching for our 4k tail? i want a ballpark for capacity planning.
[05:36] Alex Chen: sure. for 4k tail sessions with prefix+kv caching and dynamic batching (50ms cap) we measured: effective tokens/$ ~2.7m when including compute+15% infra overhead. tokens/sec per GPU equivalently was around 18k tokens/sec sustained with batching; per-dollar numbers scale with reserved pricing but that's the run-level number.
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: 18k tokens/sec — is that per-gpu? what's your assumed GPU model?
[05:59] Alex Chen: p4d equivalent, yes — depending on instance type p5/4/gh100 numbers vary but we normalize to p4d for the sheet. we can give raw numbers by instance type if you want.
[06:10] Sana Rizvi: do we have any bench with 2 x requests per second with 100 concurrent users? our load shape is bursty, not steady; i'm worried about cold start behavior and concurrency spikes.
[06:19] Alex Chen: cold start is mostly warmed once KV is populated; for bursty loads we recommend a small warm pool and autoscale policy tuned for burst capacity. warm pool keeps model warmed and reduces tail latency on spikes. we measured cold start penalty of ~400–600ms on a full model spinup, warm pool removed that.
[06:42] Maya Patel: quick check — any talk of compliance or SOC2 this week? diego we did share the security pack last week — any outstanding items?
[06:49] Diego Morales: we got it, just need clarifications on key rotation and HSM support for private deployments. no blocker for cost work.
[06:55] Alex Chen: noted — i'll loop in our infra security lead for the HSM Qs.
[06:59] Maya Patel: ok back to economics — let's sketch the main optimization paths: 1) caching + prefix rewrite 2) dynamic batching 3) selective cheap-variant routing 4) reserved capacity once utilization justifies it 5) fine-tune q config for QA tolerance. prioritized by ROI.
[07:16] Liam O'Connor: makes sense. can you quantify ROI order-of-magnitude? like first two give X% cost drop?
[07:21] Alex Chen: based on our runs: prefix+kv caching delivered ~25–40% cost reduction depending on session mix; dynamic batching another ~30–50% relative to batch=1 depending on latency caps; cheap-variant routing another 20–45% on eligible traffic. combined you can see 2–3x improvement tokens/$. so near term focus should be caching and latency-aware batching.
[07:43] Sana Rizvi: what's the ops work to enable prefix caching? needs infra changes on our side?
[07:47] Alex Chen: minimal — you need to tag common prefixes at the app layer or send a prefix-hash flag; Redwood runtime will persist and reuse cached embeddings/kv for identical prefixes. we'll share sample code.
[07:56] Maya Patel: ok next let's agree on concrete next benchmark: alex?
[07:59] Alex Chen: propose we run a 4k-context benchmark with your production distribution: three configs — (A) baseline q4_k no caching batch1, (B) q4_k + caching + dynamic batch (50ms cap), (C) q4_k + caching + routing to 1.3b for templated prompts. we'll report tokens/sec, tokens/$ (compute+15% infra), p50/p95/p99 latencies, and accuracy deltas on your eval set. target finish by Tue 2026-06-30.
[08:27] Liam O'Connor: that sounds good. also please surface the per-request cost model so finance can map to projected monthly spend.
[08:33] Maya Patel: maya to send updated pricing sheet and caching guide today. alex to run the benchmarks and post results and raw logs in the shared drive by 6/30. liam to provide anonymized request distribution dump and evaluation set.
[08:45] Diego Morales: we will try to provide logs by 6/26.
[08:48] Sana Rizvi: any final questions on tradeoffs?
[08:50] Liam O'Connor: only one — do we have a simple formula to explain tokens/$ to exec? something like tokens per GPU-hour and GPU-hour per dollar?
[08:57] Alex Chen: yes we include a simple KPI in the sheet: tokens per GPU-hour and tokens per dollar = tokens per GPU-hour / $ per GPU-hour. we'll add example rows for your planned volume.
[09:07] Maya Patel: ok recap of action items and next meeting.
[09:10] Maya Patel: action items = maya send pricing and caching guide; alex run 3-config benchmark and upload results by 6/30; liam share request distribution and eval set by 6/26; diego/sana follow up on HSM clarifications — alex to loop in security lead. next sync one week, 2026-07-01 same time.
[09:29] Diego Morales: thanks all.
[09:31] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in chat. bye.
next_steps: Alex Chen to run 3-config 4k-context benchmark and upload results to shared drive by 2026-06-30
Maya Patel to send updated pricing sheet and caching guide by 2026-06-25
Liam O'Connor to provide anonymized request distribution and eval set by 2026-06-26
